sections.h2: What should a Christian County, KY homeowner know about property tax?
sections.html:
Christian County bills follow Kentucky's statewide calendar, but the county's size and its military population shape how selling works. It is the second-largest county in Kentucky by area at 724 square miles and the largest in the western part of the state. Hopkinsville is the seat, and the other cities are Crofton, LaFayette, Oak Grove and Pembroke.

The county was formed in 1797, and the present courthouse dates to 1869, replacing one burned in 1864. It sits in the Central time zone and belongs to the Clarksville metropolitan area, with Tennessee counties along its southern edge.

sections.h2: Who do I call in Christian County for each tax or records task?
sections.html:
Most of what a seller needs runs through the county clerk's office at 511 South Main Street in Hopkinsville, which is open Monday to Friday from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. The clerk's own phone menu sorts the common tasks.

Christian County Clerk phone routing for sellers (county website)
What you needNumberNotes
Main clerk line(270) 887-4105Menu extension 3 covers copies of a deed or a plat
Legal records division(270) 887-4109Deeds, mortgages, tax liens and releases filed since 1797
Delinquent tax sale questions(270) 887-4109Number given for the tax sale registration notice
Probate and court records(270) 889-6539Justice Center, not the clerk

For the value of your house, contact the Christian County PVA. For the amount of this year's bill, contact the sheriff's tax office. If you cannot find a current number, ask the clerk's main line to direct you.

sections.h2: How does the Christian County housing market affect a tax sale?
sections.html:
Christian County has an unusual split. The 2020 census counted 26,435 households and 29,206 housing units, with 49.9 percent of occupied homes owned and 50.1 percent rented. The median age was 30.0, and 9.5 percent of units were vacant. About 71 percent of residents lived in urban areas.

Rentals make up half of occupied homes, so many sellers here are landlords. If you own a rental, the tax bill is yours to pay even when a tenant is in the unit, and unpaid tax follows the parcel into any sale. Schools are mostly Christian County Public Schools, while Fort Campbell residents are zoned to the federal DoDEA schools. Hopkinsville Community College and regional Murray State campuses are also in the county.

  • Tornadoes crossed northern Christian County in 2006 and 2008 and damaged homes around Crofton.
  • The 2017 eclipse reached its greatest point in the Bainbridge and Sinking Fork area, on a farm, which shows how much of the county is open land.
  • Fort Campbell North is a census-designated place inside the county.

sections.h2: What are the Christian County tax payment dates and penalties?
sections.html:
Kentucky law, not a local rule, fixes the schedule. KRS 134.015 gives a 2 percent discount for paying the full bill by November 1, then the plain bill amount through December 31. A 5 percent penalty runs through January 31, and 10 percent applies after that date.

The sheriff adds a fee of its own for late payment, which is why the Department of Revenue's examples show a $1,000 bill reaching $1,254 when it moves to the clerk: the 10 percent penalty, a sheriff add-on and a sheriff commission. If your home is inside Hopkinsville, Oak Grove or another city, ask that city whether it bills its own tax and on what dates.

If you are a landlord, pay early. The discount alone is worth 2 percent on every rental in your portfolio.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Christian County assessment?
sections.html:
Book a conference with the Christian County PVA while the tax roll is open for inspection. Kentucky law lets you ask for the conference by telephone, and the PVA must explain how your value was reached.

If that fails, file a written appeal with the county clerk by one workday after the inspection period ends. The county board of assessment appeals sits 25 to 35 days after that. Your petition should name the parcel and give your opinion of its fair cash value, and the board relies on evidence such as comparable sales, contracts, insurance policies and, for rentals, income and expense statements. Anyone who is paid to represent you must be an attorney, accountant, tax consultant, licensed broker, appraiser or your own employee, with written authority.

  • The board can raise a value as well as lower it, so bring evidence for your number.
  • After the county board, further appeals go to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.
  • An appeal does not delay payment of tax on the value you claim.

sections.h2: When is the Christian County delinquent tax sale?
sections.html:
The clerk holds one each summer. For the most recent cycle, the county website set the delinquent property tax sale for July 28, 2026 at 9:00 am Central, with participants required to register by close of business on July 20, 2026. Both dates have passed, and the next sale will follow the same summer timing.

Behind the sale is a state timetable. Unpaid bills transfer to the clerk on April 15, and a county sale must fall at least 90 days but not more than 135 days after that transfer. Before then, the county attorney mails notices, and the clerk advertises the list at least 30 days ahead. A buyer who wants more than three bills in the county, or more than five statewide, has to register with the Department of Revenue 60 days before the sale.

Paying before the sale ends the matter. Paying after leaves you owing the new lien holder.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Kentucky homestead exemption in Christian County?
sections.html:
Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and who live in the home. The Department of Revenue lists the exemption at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, subtracted from the assessed value before tax is calculated. File with the Christian County PVA and bring proof of age or disability. Disability claims need yearly renewal, except for service-connected veterans and owners with permanent disability findings from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

Ask the PVA how a move, or renting the house out, affects the exemption before you change how the property is used.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Christian County house that owes taxes?
sections.html:
Get payoff figures first, then price the house with them in mind. The sheriff's tax office can state the balance on a current bill, and the clerk can confirm whether any older year was filed as a certificate of delinquency. Both amounts come out of the sale price at closing, and the title company records the release.

Moves tied to Fort Campbell can leave little time, and tax penalties keep running on the statutory dates. A buyer who purchases as-is can close on the date you need, and the tax lines are paid from your proceeds. That is often easier than catching up in cash while you are packing.

faqs.q: What is the county clerk's address in Christian County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The clerk is at 511 South Main Street, Hopkinsville, KY 42240, phone (270) 887-4105, open Monday to Friday 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. The legal records division is at (270) 887-4109.

faqs.q: When did Christian County hold its 2026 delinquent tax sale?
faqs.a: The county website scheduled it for July 28, 2026 at 9:00 am Central, with registration due July 20, 2026. Those dates are past.

faqs.q: What happens to a Christian County tax bill after April 15?
faqs.a: It moves from the sheriff to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a lien on the property. Interest of 1 percent a month and clerk and attorney fees are then added.

faqs.q: Do I still owe tax if a renter lives in my Christian County house?
faqs.a: Yes. Property tax is the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, no matter who occupies the house.

faqs.q: Is a Christian County homeowner over 65 eligible for a reduction?
faqs.a: Yes, through the homestead exemption, which was $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. Apply with the Christian County PVA and show proof of age.
